newsitem.title: GERMANY: Modern teenagers are tough consumers - German survey.
newsitem.headline: Modern teenagers are tough consumers - German survey.

text.p: Anti-consumerist Generation X-ers have given way to a hedonistic class of 1990s teenagers in Germany, the German unit of advertising group Grey said on Tuesday based on a study it conducted.
"Teenagers today are no longer rebels," Grey said in a summary of its findings. "The main thing they want is to somehow have some fun."
The group said it had undertaken the "Teens 2000" survey to find out how 13 to 19 year-old Germans spend their estimated seven billion marks ($3.7 billion) of disposable income every year.

While those in their 20s and early 30s, the so-called Generation X, have rejected advertising and mass consumption in large numbers, Grey said teenagers today have become media and advertising experts, using or ignoring offers at their will.
"Teenagers have grown up with channel and Internet surfing and media inundation so they have learned to weed through the growing mass quantity," Grey said.
"They are demanding, critical and sometimes merciless in terms of messages and campaigns, but they enjoy being courted and entertained," he said.
